newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's phosphate firm profit up to $87 mln/1996.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's phosphate firm profit up to $87 mln/1996.

text.p: Morocco's state-owned phosphates giant Office Cherifien des Phosphates (OCP) registered a pre-tax profit of 800 million dirhams ($87 million) in 1996, against a deficit of 14 million dirhams ($1.5 million) in 1995, a spokesman said on Thursday.

"The improvement of phosphate price by $4 a tonne on the world market and adjustment of the enterprise policy were behind the 800 million pretax profit made by OCP in 1996," a spokesman at the Casablanca-based office said.
The firm registered losses of 14 million dirhams in 1995, he said.

The release of these figures coincided with the meeting of OCP board of directors which was presided by Prime Minister Abdellatif Filali on Thursday. The meeting examined the firm's activities in 1995/1996, the official MAP news agency said.
"OCP plans to invest the amount of 10.7 billion dirhams in a three-year plan ending in 2001," the agency said.
Phosphates output reached 20.8 million tonnes in 1996, slightly up from 20.3 million tonnes in 1995, MAP said.
Raw phosphate exports rose 7.6 percent in 1996, to go beyond the line of 10 million tonnes in 1996, it added.

OCP turnover was $1.4 billion in 1996, up from $1.2 billion in the previous year. The company, Morocco's main job provider, with 27,700 employees, including 750 engineers, is the world's first raw phosphate exporter.
The conglomerate's debt burden have slightly declined in the last two years but remains high, the office said.
"OCP debt dropped to 11.6 billion dirhams in 1996 from 21.8 billion dirhams in 1994...It is expected to be reduced to 1.5 billion dirhams by the year 2001 or 10 percent of turnover," it said.
The office paid back the amount of 2.3 billion dirhams to the state treasury in 1996, it added.
